lead: From industrial Poblenou to the Vila Olímpica: beaches, innovation and new neighbourhoods by the sea.
history: Sant Martí de Provençals was an independent municipality until 1897. Its best-known neighbourhood, El Poblenou, was the most industrial area in Catalonia in the late 19th century, the "Catalan Manchester", and today it is home to the 22@ innovation district, with old factories reborn as lofts, studios and offices.

The 1992 Olympic Games opened the city to the sea with the Vila Olímpica and the beaches, and Diagonal Mar and the Fòrum completed the transformation of the coast. Its ten neighbourhoods combine converted factories, new-build developments, seafront towers and the blocks of flats of the inland neighbourhoods.

Across its 10 neighbourhoods, the average sale price ranges from 2,837 €/m² in El Besòs i el Maresme to 5,528 €/m² in Diagonal Mar i el Front Marítim del Poblenou, and the average rent from 756 €/month in El Besòs i el Maresme to 1,732 €/month in Diagonal Mar i el Front Marítim del Poblenou.
Prices and atmosphere change a great deal between the seafront and the inland neighbourhoods, so it is worth comparing each area carefully.
summary: Sant Martí has 252,625 inhabitants in 10.44 km² and 10 neighbourhoods. Its average sale price was 4,115 €/m² in 2025, 3% below the city average. The average rent is 1,094 €/month.
